branches.before_mutation: Readable returns the supplied IReadOnlyList<T>; Contains and IndexOf enumerate it and call static object.Equals.
branches.first_mutation: Writable constructs new List<T>(_source). Add, Clear, Insert, Remove, RemoveAt, or an indexer setter can trigger this.
branches.after_mutation: Readable returns _copy, but Contains and IndexOf still enumerate through IReadOnlyList<T> and still call static object.Equals.
branches.existing_remove: Remove delegates to List<T>.Remove, whose default typed equality is not a precedent for changing Contains/IndexOf.

consumer_contract: MvcOptions.ValueProviderFactories is IList<IValueProviderFactory>, initialized as List<IValueProviderFactory>.
ControllerContext.ValueProviderFactories exposes IList<IValueProviderFactory> for the current request.
ControllerActionInvoker passes the same list into ResourceInvoker; ResourceInvoker constructs ResourceExecutingContext with that list.
ResourceExecutingContext exposes that same list to real resource filters; modifications are request-local.
CompositeValueProvider.CreateAsync consumes factories by Count/indexer and invokes CreateValueProviderAsync, not Contains/IndexOf.
A struct registered as an IValueProviderFactory is stored via an interface reference; it does not change the collection's generic argument to the struct type.

documentation.contract: Default checks whether the type T implements IEquatable<T>; if so it uses that implementation, otherwise it uses Object.Equals/Object.GetHashCode overrides.
documentation.consequence: A concrete IEquatable<T> class or struct can differ from static object.Equals. A runtime factory implementing IEquatable of its concrete type does not make the generic interface IValueProviderFactory implement IEquatable<IValueProviderFactory>.
